skill.name: set-up-shopware-meta-poas-bidding
skill.description: Set up profit or revenue bidding in Meta for a Shopware 6.7 store using Product Metrics. Check tracking, verify a test order, and plan a value-based bidding target.
skill.summary: Use Shopware order profit to guide Meta bidding through Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Most scanner hits are Markdown, routine setup checks, or descriptions of expected integration behavior. Seven flags reflect real risks involving configuration writes, order-data access, an unpinned installer, broad MCP execution, or mutable remote instructions. Separate findings cover token exposure, inconsistent consent guidance, and overstated break-even claims; no evidence of malware or audit-directed prompt injection was found.

remediation.issue: Meta access tokens may pass through the assistant or tool interface.
remediation.suggestion: Require users to enter Meta access tokens directly in the Product Metrics app. Remove instructions to request or pass raw tokens through chat or command arguments.

remediation.issue: Product Metrics writes and remote MCP actions lack explicit approval boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Limit the agent to named, scoped read operations by default. Require approval of the workspace, property, destination, and exact change before any write.

remediation.issue: Order validation may access more customer and business data than needed.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the workspace and sales channel. Use a known test order and report delivery status without exposing order details or using a broad order listing.

remediation.issue: The installation command does not pin the installer or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Pin a reviewed installer version and skill commit. Present the installation as a separate user-approved step.

remediation.issue: Live documentation can replace the reviewed reference instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle versioned references. Treat any fetched documentation as untrusted guidance that cannot authorize tools, writes, or new destinations.

remediation.issue: The overview does not consistently disclose consent requirements for profit events.
remediation.suggestion: State both consent requirements before enabling the destination. Verify that denied consent suppresses profit events and disclose which customer fields Meta receives.

remediation.issue: The documented ROAS target can overstate actual profitability.
remediation.suggestion: Label the target as a reported-value benchmark. Check realized contribution margin, including losses and later refunds, before making profitability claims or scaling spend.

semantic_findings.title: Meta Access Token Requested Through Assistant
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the assistant to obtain the Meta access token and pass it to a command. This can expose it through chat or tool records.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The reference recommends app entry but also says the assistant must ask for the token. The skill accepts it without specifying a protected input channel.

semantic_findings.title: Profit Tracking Overview Omits Consent Conditions
semantic_findings.description: The overview says every paid order sends profit and that each event carries hashed customer data. Other sections require both marketing and analytics consent for profit events.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The overview is broader than the documented consent rules and omits other matching fields. No evidence found that the plugin ignores consent.

semantic_findings.title: Reported Profit Target Can Overstate Break-Even
semantic_findings.description: The guidance treats a 100% target as break-even. Meta bidding values floor losses at zero, and later refunds do not revise the reported events.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented bidding value can exceed realized contribution profit. Covering ad spend in Meta reporting does not establish that the campaign broke even.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding in Meta for Shopware
content.value_statement: A Meta campaign can meet its revenue target and still lose money. This skill guides you through using Shopware order profit as a bidding signal in Meta.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP and identify incomplete steps.
Guide pairing a Shopware sales channel and connecting the correct Meta pixel or dataset.
Explain how Shopware purchase prices and additional costs determine which orders have a profit value.
Guide validation of a consented test order and creation of a profit custom conversion in Meta.
Compare revenue and profit bidding targets and suggest a starting target from observed profit on ad spend.
limitations: Requires Product Metrics Pro and a supported Shopware 6.7 installation with PHP 8.2 or later.
A person must complete Shopware admin steps and select the optimization event in Meta.
Profit events require complete costs and both marketing and analytics consent.
Historical orders are not imported into Meta, and later refunds do not revise sent events.

use_cases.title: Check Store Readiness
use_cases.description: Identify what remains before a paired Shopware sales channel can send order profit to the correct Meta dataset.

use_cases.title: Plan a Profit Bidding Pilot
use_cases.description: Choose one Meta campaign for a trial and compare a profit-based goal with the current revenue-based goal.

use_cases.title: Validate Conversion Delivery
use_cases.description: Use a test order to check event delivery and distinguish missing costs from consent or test mode issues.

prompt_templates.title: Explain Profit Bidding
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how profit bidding differs from revenue bidding for my Shopware store. List the prerequisites and do not connect to any account.

prompt_templates.title: Review Setup Status
prompt_templates.prompt: Review setup for my selected Product Metrics property without making changes. Tell me which Shopware or Meta steps I need to complete.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a Missing Profit Event
prompt_templates.prompt: My test order shows revenue but no profit event in Meta. Help me check consent, cost completeness, and test mode without retrieving unrelated orders.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Campaign Pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: plan a switch from revenue to profit.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a one-campaign pilot using observed profit on ad spend of 1.5. Explain the custom conversion, starting target, and margin checks without changing any campaign.

output_examples.input: Why does my test order show revenue but no profit?
output: Check whether all product and additional costs are present. A test order with an unknown cost can arrive with revenue only.
Confirm the test order has marketing and analytics consent, then check the profit event in Meta Test events.

output_examples.input: What target should I test if my current profit on ad spend is 1.5?
output: Use 150% as a starting target for one campaign. Select the custom conversion based on the order profit event in Meta.
Check realized margin before extending the test. Meta reports losses as zero in the bidding value and does not revise events after later refunds.

best_practices: Verify the sales channel and Meta dataset before enabling any data transfer.
Enter the Meta access token directly in Product Metrics and keep it out of chat.
Validate a consented test order, then clear the test event code before checking live reporting.
anti_patterns: Do not carry a revenue-based target unchanged into a campaign that bids on profit.
Do not enable all Shopware sales channels when pairing a single storefront.
Do not assume Meta reports net profitability after losses and later refunds.

faq.question: What is POAS?
faq.answer: Profit on ad spend is contribution profit divided by ad spend. ROAS uses revenue instead of profit.

faq.question: Can I keep bidding on revenue?
faq.answer: Yes. Use the standard Purchase event, which carries revenue, and set a revenue-based goal.

faq.question: Why is the profit event missing from Meta?
faq.answer: Meta must receive the event before it appears in the selector. Check cost completeness and both analytics and marketing consent before testing again.

faq.question: Does one installation track every sales channel?
faq.answer: No. One installation tracks paid orders from the single sales channel you pair.

faq.question: What customer data does Meta receive?
faq.answer: With marketing consent, Meta receives hashed email, name, postal code, and country, plus IP address and browser information. Browser identifiers also require ad storage consent.

faq.question: Does Meta import past orders or apply later refunds?
faq.answer: No. The integration does not backfill past orders, and Meta events are not revised when an order is later refunded.
